\subsubsection{Train-Time Ablation: Endpoint Statistics}
\label{app:train_time_ablation}

Table~\ref{tab:train_time_ablation} gives the endpoint statistics of the curves in
Figure~\ref{fig:train_time_ablation}, using the same conventions as Table~\ref{tab:rlhammer}. The undefended base and
SR-Agent rows repeat the Qwen3-8B entries of that table and are the mean of two independent attacker trainings; the two
ablation rows are single attacker trainings against the model trained without reflection, and differ only in the
target's thinking mode, which is held consistent between attacker training and target evaluation.

The two ablation settings end at the same point, $60.0\%$, within a point of the undefended base's $59.5\%$ and roughly
three and a half times SR-Agent's $17.0\%$. That the two settings agree is what makes the row interpretable: the model
trained without reflection is equally exposed whether or not it is asked to think at inference, so its vulnerability
follows from the missing reflection supervision rather than from any distribution shift introduced at evaluation time.
The remaining difference between the two is in shape rather than level --- with thinking enabled the attacker reaches
its peak earlier (epoch 12 against epoch 20) --- which is why the Last-5 means differ slightly while the final values
do not.
